task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 31, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer about Elmward Components' first profit-sharing payment, answering how the pool is divided and why a payment is not the same as owning company stock.

facts.text: Elmward Components announced its first annual profit-sharing pool in August 2026 for the financial year ended June 30.
The plan allocates 10% of eligible operating profit before the profit-sharing expense to employee payments.
The company's supplied calculation uses $400,000 of eligible operating profit, producing a $40,000 pool.
That figure is not described as after-tax net profit, and the packet does not provide every adjustment from the company's full accounts.
Thirty eligible employees receive one allocation unit each and 20 eligible half-time employees receive half a unit each, totaling 40 units.
The pool therefore pays $1,000 per full unit and $500 per half unit, before individual deductions.
Of the company's 57 employees, seven had not completed six months of service by the plan's June 30, 2026, eligibility cutoff and do not share in this payout.
The payment will appear separately from base wages in November payroll and does not change hourly wage rates.
The plan transfers no shares, votes or ownership rights to recipients.
A future year with no eligible profit would produce no pool under the supplied formula.
The current payout is therefore not a guaranteed recurring addition to annual wages.
Finance manager Rella Gant says eligibility and allocation were checked against the payroll records for the covered year.
Gant said, "Sharing a result is different from changing who owns the company."
Assembly worker Omi Vale welcomes the payment but says regular wage rates remain important for budgeting ordinary bills.
Vale said, "I can use a bonus when it arrives. I cannot put next year's unknown profit on a monthly payment plan."
Employees will receive individual calculation notices and can ask payroll to review their recorded allocation unit.
The plan does not let employees demand a sale of the business or cash out an ownership stake.
The company has not published an independent audit of the full plan calculation or a measured productivity effect.
Elmward makes fittings for industrial shelving and has operated from the same estate since 2003.
The founders retain ownership under the announcement; no worker buyout or outside acquisition is proposed.

forbidden_additions: Employees receive stock, voting rights or a guaranteed annual bonus
All 57 employees receive $1,000 or the $400,000 is verified after-tax net profit
